title: Fix missing root element binding and JavaScript errors causing blank white page

requirements.summary: Verify and add root div element in frontend/index.html
acceptanceCriteria:
The frontend/index.html file contains
in the body
The root div is the only child element in the body before the script tag
No other elements interfere with React mounting

file_operations.description:
Verify that the body section contains a div element with id='root'. If missing or malformed, add or fix it with the exact markup:
. Ensure this div is the only child element in the body before the script tag that loads main.tsx. Remove any conflicting elements that might interfere with React mounting.

requirements.summary: Add null checks and error handling for root element mounting in frontend/src/main.tsx
acceptanceCriteria: The createRoot call uses document.getElementById('root')
Code checks if rootElement is null before calling createRoot
If root element is missing, logs detailed error to console
If root element is missing, displays visible error message on page using document.body.innerHTML

file_operations.description: Modify the root element targeting to use document.getElementById('root') with a null check. If the rootElement is null, log a detailed error message to console.error explaining that the root element is missing, and display a visible error message directly to the page using document.body.innerHTML with red background and white text. Only proceed with createRoot if the element exists.

requirements.summary: Add comprehensive try-catch blocks around React initialization in frontend/src/main.tsx
acceptanceCriteria: Try-catch wraps the entire React mounting logic
Caught errors are logged with console.error including stack trace
Error message is displayed visibly on the page using document.body.innerHTML with red background
Error display includes the error message text and component name that failed

file_operations.description: Wrap the ReactDOM.createRoot and root.render calls in a comprehensive try-catch block. In the catch block, log the full error with stack trace using console.error, and display a user-visible error message directly to document.body.innerHTML with red background styling. Include the error message text and indicate which component or initialization step failed.

requirements.summary: Add execution tracing console logs in frontend/src/main.tsx
acceptanceCriteria: Console log appears before any import statements
Console log appears immediately before createRoot call
Logs include timestamp or execution order markers
Logs are visible in browser developer console

file_operations.description: Add console.log('main.tsx: Script loaded') at the very beginning of the file before any import statements. Add console.log('main.tsx: About to mount React app') immediately before the createRoot call. Include timestamps or execution order markers in the logs to trace execution flow. These logs should be visible in the browser developer console.

requirements.summary: Verify and add error handling for import resolution in frontend/src/main.tsx
acceptanceCriteria: All import paths are correct and files exist
No circular dependency issues between imported modules
Module resolution errors are caught and logged with specific import that failed
Fallback error UI displays if critical imports fail

file_operations.description: Verify that all import statements (React, ReactDOM, App component, QueryClientProvider, InternetIdentityProvider) resolve correctly. Check that import paths are correct and the imported files exist. Add try-catch around the main execution block to catch any module resolution errors during runtime. Log specific import failures with console.error including which module failed to load. Display a fallback error UI if critical imports fail to load.

requirements.summary: Add defensive initialization checks to InternetIdentityProvider in frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts
acceptanceCriteria: InternetIdentityProvider component has try-catch around initialization logic
Errors during auth setup do not prevent app from rendering
Failed authentication gracefully falls back to logged-out state
Error details are logged to console for debugging

file_operations.description: Wrap the InternetIdentityProvider component's initialization logic in try-catch blocks, particularly around AuthClient creation and any async authentication calls. Ensure that errors during auth setup do not throw uncaught exceptions that would prevent the app from rendering. If authentication initialization fails, gracefully fall back to an unauthenticated state and log detailed error information to console.error for debugging. The app should still render even if Internet Identity setup fails.

requirements.summary: Verify App component export and add isolation test in frontend/src/App.tsx
acceptanceCriteria: App component has proper export default declaration
Simplified App component renders successfully without child components
Console logs confirm App component function executes
Visible text appears on screen confirming React is mounted

file_operations.description: Verify that the App component has a proper 'export default' declaration. Add a console.log statement at the beginning of the App component function to confirm it executes. Temporarily simplify the App component to render a minimal test UI (a simple div displaying 'App component loaded successfully') to isolate and verify that React mounting works. This diagnostic change helps identify whether the issue is in the mounting process or in child components. Once verified working, the full component implementation can be restored.
